title: Locally closed images of field groupoid morphisms are closed
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], put $V=\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $(V,R_1,s_1,t_1,e_1,i_1,c_1)$ and $(V,R_2,s_2,t_2,e_2,i_2,c_2)$ be absolute groupoid schemes [def-a1-groupoid-scheme]. Suppose $a:R_1\to R_2$ together with $\mathrm{id}_V$ commutes with the source, target, unit, inverse and composition maps. If the image $a(|R_1|)$ is locally closed in $|R_2|$ (the intersection of an open and a closed subset), then it is closed. In particular, if $a$ is an immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], then $a$ is a closed immersion.

source.place: Tag 04Q9 (lemma-locally-closed-image-is-closed), Situation 04Q5 (situation-morphism-groupoids-on-field); final assertion uses schemes.tex Tag 01IQ (lemma-immersion-when-closed).

proof.text: Put $I=a(|R_1|)$. Apply [lem-sfb-field-groupoid-perfect-restriction], obtaining the perfect field $k^{\prime}$, morphism $a^{\prime}$ and homeomorphisms $q_1,q_2$. Commutativity and surjectivity of $q_1$ give $q_2(a^{\prime}(|R_1^{\prime}|))=I$. Since $q_2$ is bijective, $a^{\prime}(|R_1^{\prime}|)=q_2^{-1}(I)$. Thus this image is locally closed, and it is closed if and only if $I$ is closed, since a homeomorphism preserves open and closed sets. It suffices to prove the assertion over $k^{\prime}$; rename it $k$, so henceforth $k$ is perfect.

By [lem-sfb-perfect-field-groupoid-image-closure] let $j:Z\hookrightarrow R_2$ be the reduced closure groupoid of $I$. Apply the same result to $\mathrm{id}_{R_1}$, obtaining the groupoid $A=(R_1)_{\mathrm{red}}$ and its inclusion $r:A\hookrightarrow R_1$. The map $a\circ r$ has image $I\subseteq |Z|$, since reduction is the identity on underlying sets [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction]. Its source $A$ is reduced. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-source-factors-through-closed-subscheme] supplies $b:A\to Z$ with $j\circ b=a\circ r$. Its image in $Z$ is exactly $I$.

source.place: Tag 04Q9, second proof paragraph, correcting the printed R2-red to R1-red.

proof.text: The map $(\mathrm{id}_V,b)$ is a groupoid morphism. Indeed $j b=a r$ gives the source and target equations immediately. For unit, inverse and composition, composing the required equations with $j$ gives the corresponding equations for $a,r,j$, which are groupoid morphisms. Cancel $j$: a closed immersion is injective on morphisms from every test scheme, because on its affine quotient charts a ring map out of a quotient is determined by its composite with the surjective quotient map; the local equalities glue. This proves the three remaining operation equations, including on $A\times_{s_A,V,t_A}A$. These are precisely the equations in [def-a1-groupoid-scheme].

source.place: Tag 04Q9, second proof paragraph; explicit verification of the factorized groupoid morphism.

proof.text: Write $I=O\cap C$ with $O$ open and $C$ closed in $|R_2|$. Since $I\subseteq C$, its closure $|Z|$ is contained in $C$; thus $I=O\cap |Z|$ is open in $|Z|$. The morphism $b$ of step 3 has this open image. Apply [lem-sfb-field-groupoid-open-image-closed] to $b:A\to Z$: its image $I$ is closed in $|Z|$. It is dense there by the definition $|Z|=\overline I$. Hence $I=|Z|$, which is closed in $|R_2|$. Step 1 now gives the original assertion over the original field.

source.place: Tag 04Q9, second proof paragraph, application of 04Q6 and density.

proof.text: Finally assume $a$ is an immersion. By [def-weil-closed-immersion] it factors as a closed immersion into an open subscheme of $R_2$. Its image is therefore closed in that open subset, hence locally closed in $|R_2|$. The assertion just proved makes it closed in $|R_2|$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-closed-image-closed-immersion] to conclude that $a$ is a closed immersion.

source.place: Tag 04Q9, conclusion, followed by schemes.tex Tag 01IQ (lemma-immersion-when-closed).
